Just an immunocompromised bean living in an unsafe world 🌎❤️‍🩹🦠😷 1) Not all bodies react the same to viruses. Some immune systems are stronger/weaker than others due to age and underlying health conditions. Exposure to viruses does not help immune systems, getting covid has made mine worse; get vaccinated instead. 2) Even if you are healthy, viruses still pose a risk. I was healthy, young and fit before a virus made me chronically ill. 3) There is no cure and little understanding of post-viral illnesses.  4) Its not a case of “you do you”. This doesn’t apply to drink driving or smoking indoors because these impact the health and safety of others. Viruses get transmitted in the air and via surfaces. We have a duty to protect each other.  5) We need safety precautions like wearing a mask on public transport and in medical spaces, wearing a mask in public when you have a virus you can transmit in the air, prioritising hygiene LONG-TERM. If you’ve been struck with a cold or suffering with flu symptoms or like me just want to give your immune system some extra TLC then try making a batch of my healing turmeric & ginger tonic this week, keep it in the fridge and drink it daily to give you a natural boost. It’s loaded with anti-inflammatories, it’s sweet and tasty and basically exactly what the doctor ordered! Ingredients 3 inches of turmeric root 3 inches ginger root Juice of one lemon Zest of quarter orange peel 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup (skip this if you don’t fancy the sweetness) Pinch of pepper (to enhance the bioavailability of the turmeric ✨) 500ml water to make 2 big mugs or double up and boil 1litre of water to make a batch of healing tonic for the week ahead. I usually do this and pour half of the turmeric tonic mixture into a cup and fill the rest with boiling water to make it stretch. Method 1. Chop the turmeric & ginger, add to pan of water on medium heat along with the lemon juice, honey, orange zest & pinch of fresh black pepper 2. Bring to the boil and then allow to simmer for 10 mins 3. Pour through a sieve into a jug and then serve your tonic in mugs with a slice of lemon or orange 4. If making a bigger batch then leave the rest to cool & then pour through a sieve and transfer into an airtight bottle and keep fresh in the fridge. TIP: Support your body by drinking a cup or multiple cups everyday that you’re feeling run-down and to make it stretch (this batch lasts about 5 days) by filling your mug half with your pre-made tonic and the rest with hot water to get more out of your tonic (and to save time during the week). #immuneboost #flu #tonic #healthyfood

If you’ve been struck with a cold or suffering with flu symptoms or like me just want to give your immune system some extra TLC then try making a batch of my healing turmeric & ginger tonic this week, keep it in the fridge and drink it daily to give you a natural boost. It’s loaded with anti-inflammatories, it’s sweet and tasty and basically exactly what the doctor ordered! Ingredients 3 inches of turmeric root 3 inches ginger root Juice of one lemon Zest of quarter orange peel 1 tbsp honey or maple syrup (skip this if you don’t fancy the sweetness) Pinch of pepper (to enhance the bioavailability of the turmeric ✨) 500ml water to make 2 big mugs or double up and boil 1litre of water to make a batch of healing tonic for the week ahead. I usually do this and pour half of the turmeric tonic mixture into a cup and fill the rest with boiling water to make it stretch. Method 1. Chop the turmeric & ginger, add to pan of water on medium heat along with the lemon juice, honey, orange zest & pinch of fresh black pepper 2. Bring to the boil and then allow to simmer for 10 mins 3. Pour through a sieve into a jug and then serve your tonic in mugs with a slice of lemon or orange 4. If making a bigger batch then leave the rest to cool & then pour through a sieve and transfer into an airtight bottle and keep fresh in the fridge. TIP: Support your body by drinking a cup or multiple cups everyday that you’re feeling run-down and to make it stretch (this batch lasts about 5 days) by filling your mug half with your pre-made tonic and the rest with hot water to get more out of your tonic (and to save time during the week). #immuneboost #flu #tonic #healthyfood

Starbucks’ turmeric latte is not the one 🙅🏽‍♀️ Did you know that turmeric latte AKA haldi dudh originated in India? And the OG haldi dudh is WAYYYY more delicious and beneficial to our health than the Starbucks version. We use it as a natural home remedy for a sore throat, coughs and colds, fighting inflammation…just about anything. Turmeric is an amazing anti-inflammatory with high antioxidant levels, cancer fighting properties, anti ageing properties (hence why we smear turmeric paste on the bodies and faces of people getting married 🌝) and so much more. The main difference between real haldi dudh and Starbucks’ turmeric latte: cooking the turmeric beforehand. Skip this step and you’ll end up with the Starbucks version; it doesn’t taste good and the turmeric doesn’t mix with the milk. Cooking turmeric for a short time (30 seconds) allows it to become more soluble so it will dissolve easier into your milk and also absorb into your body easier. The anti inflammatory and antioxidant properties increase with slight cooking, and plus the flavour mellows and it tastes way better. Haldi dudh (1 cup) 1 tsp butter / ghee / coconut oil (I make mine vegan so I use coconut oil) Once melted add 1/2 tsp turmeric Cook until it browns slightly (30 seconds) and add milk of choice Ayurvedic constitution: if suitable for you, you can add spices like cinnamon and black pepper You can also add sugar, coconut sugar, maple/carob syrup etc. Never add honey to a hot drink or heat honey! When honey is heated it becomes toxic. Starbucks’ turmeric latte is not the one 🙅🏽‍♀️ Did you know that turmeric latte AKA haldi dudh originated in India? And the OG haldi dudh is WAYYYY more delicious and beneficial to our health than the Starbucks version. We use it as a natural home remedy for a sore throat, coughs and colds, fighting inflammation…just about anything. Turmeric is an amazing anti-inflammatory with high antioxidant levels, cancer fighting properties, anti ageing properties (hence why we smear turmeric paste on the bodies and faces of people getting married 🌝) and so much more. The main difference between real haldi dudh and Starbucks’ turmeric latte: cooking the turmeric beforehand. Skip this step and you’ll end up with the Starbucks version; it doesn’t taste good and the turmeric doesn’t mix with the milk. Cooking turmeric for a short time (30 seconds) allows it to become more soluble so it will dissolve easier into your milk and also absorb into your body easier. The anti inflammatory and antioxidant properties increase with slight cooking, and plus the flavour mellows and it tastes way better. Haldi dudh (1 cup) 1 tsp butter / ghee / coconut oil (I make mine vegan so I use coconut oil) Once melted add 1/2 tsp turmeric Cook until it browns slightly (30 seconds) and add milk of choice Ayurvedic constitution: if suitable for you, you can add spices like cinnamon and black pepper You can also add sugar, coconut sugar, maple/carob syrup etc. Never add honey to a hot drink or heat honey! When honey is heated it becomes toxic. Who is eligible for the flu vaccine in the UK: **1. People Aged 65 and Over:** All individuals aged 65 and older. **2. Pregnant Women:** Pregnant women at any stage of pregnancy. **3. Children Aged 2 to 17:** Children in this age group are typically offered the flu vaccine through a nasal spray at school or at their GP surgery. **4. People with Certain Medical Conditions:** Individuals with the following medical conditions are eligible:    - Chronic respiratory diseases (e.g., asthma or COPD).    - Chronic heart disease.    - Chronic kidney disease.    - Chronic liver disease.    - Chronic neurological diseases (e.g., Parkinson's disease or multiple sclerosis).    - Diabetes.    - Weakened immune system due to disease or treatment.    - Morbid obesity (BMI of 40 or above). **5. Healthcare Workers:** Healthcare professionals who have direct patient contact. **6. Carers:** Those who are the primary carers for someone who is elderly or disabled. **7. Frontline Social Care Workers:** Social care workers who provide direct care to clients. **8. Household Members of Shielded Patients:** People living with individuals who were previously advised to shield during the COVID-19 pandemic may be eligible. Keep in mind that eligibility criteria can change, and it's important to consult with your GP, Pharmacist or the NHS for the most current information and to confirm your eligibility for the flu vaccine. Additionally, vaccination programs may vary by region within the UK, so local health authorities should also be consulted for specific details. #fluvaccine #flujab #staywell #fluseason #nhsfluvaccine #flu #fluprevention #influenza #ukflu #diabetes #heartdisease #asthma #over65 #kidneyhealth #liverdisease

Who is eligible for the flu vaccine in the UK: **1. People Aged 65 and Over:** All individuals aged 65 and older. **2. Pregnant Women:** Pregnant women at any stage of pregnancy. **3. Children Aged 2 to 17:** Children in this age group are typically offered the flu vaccine through a nasal spray at school or at their GP surgery. **4. People with Certain Medical Conditions:** Individuals with the following medical conditions are eligible:    - Chronic respiratory diseases (e.g., asthma or COPD).    - Chronic heart disease.    - Chronic kidney disease.    - Chronic liver disease.    - Chronic neurological diseases (e.g., Parkinson's disease or multiple sclerosis).    - Diabetes.    - Weakened immune system due to disease or treatment.    - Morbid obesity (BMI of 40 or above). **5. Healthcare Workers:** Healthcare professionals who have direct patient contact. **6. Carers:** Those who are the primary carers for someone who is elderly or disabled. **7. Frontline Social Care Workers:** Social care workers who provide direct care to clients. **8. Household Members of Shielded Patients:** People living with individuals who were previously advised to shield during the COVID-19 pandemic may be eligible. Keep in mind that eligibility criteria can change, and it's important to consult with your GP, Pharmacist or the NHS for the most current information and to confirm your eligibility for the flu vaccine. Additionally, vaccination programs may vary by region within the UK, so local health authorities should also be consulted for specific details. #fluvaccine #flujab #staywell #fluseason #nhsfluvaccine #flu #fluprevention #influenza #ukflu #diabetes #heartdisease #asthma #over65 #kidneyhealth #liverdisease

Let’s talk about Vitamin C…. Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin found in citrus and other fruits and vegetables, also sold as a dietary supplement and as a topical ‘serum’ ingredient (which I use daily). With the cold weather upon us and bugs floating around it’s even more important to stock our bodies with this powerful vitamin. Here are just 7 impressive ways Vitamin C benefits our bodies… 🍊Boosts immunity. 🍊May reduce your risk of chronic disease. 🍊May help manage high blood pressure. 🍊May lower your risk of heart disease. 🍊May reduce blood uric acid levels and help prevent gout attacks. 🍊Helps prevent iron deficiency. 🍊Protects your memory and cognition as you age. Supplements have their place but it’s much more effective, where possible, to consume the actual food to get your nutrients. Here are just some fruits and vegetables that contain the best source of vitamin c all of which can be easily added into your diet: Oranges Kiwis Peppers (particularly orange) Strawberries Tomatoes Broccoli Cabbage Brussel sprouts Cauliflower Hope you find this helpful and let’s all try get our RDA of vitamin C this winter in particular to keep bugs at bay.🦠 The Recommended Dietary Allowance for adults 19 years and older is 90 mg daily for men and 75 mg for women. For pregnancy and lactation, the amount increases to 85 mg and 120 mg daily, respectively. 👀The clocks will go back on 29th October at 2am  WARNING....LONG POST🥰 Appointments available.  Message to book in.  On the last Sunday of October the clocks 'fall back': they go back by one hour. It may feel like a long time since the blue skies of summer🌞, but this marks the end of British Summer Time (BST). This will mean an extra hour in bed🛌💤💤 👣Reflexology has said to  help to rebalance the endocrine system including the #stress hormones of #cortisol and #adrenalin – high levels of these can reduce the ability to sleep or to reach a deep sleep.  #Melatonin is a hormone that is produced in the #pineal gland, the hormone rises in response to darkness and is the hormone important for #sleep and for #detoxification. 6 Benefits of Sleeping an Extra Hour💕 💕Heart protection: Sleep deprivation is associated with poor heart health because sleep influences many areas of health including #metabolism, #inflammation, and #blood pressure, all which can lead to poor heart health outcomes. Sleeping less than six hours a night has been linked to poorer #artery health. Other studies have shown lack of sleep is linked with a higher risk of heart disease and #stroke 🏋️‍♂️Stronger immune system: Your risk of catching #colds and #flu increases if you don’t sleep enough. Your body releases #cytokines when you sleep – these #proteins help fight off #viruses. If you don’t sleep well, you won’t have enough cytokines in your body to fight off #illness. 🌞Lower risk of diabetes: Lack of sleep can change your metabolism which can influence #insulin. Studies have shown sleeping less than #six hours is linked with a higher risk of type 2 #diabetes because the body produces excess insulin, but it isn’t effective at breaking down sugar. Lower risk of #depression😥: People who have trouble sleeping are at a higher risk of depression. Having sleep #apnea is also linked with a higher risk of depression. 🧠Lower risk of dementia: Although it isn’t clear if lack of sleep triggers #dementia or dementia triggers dementia, there is some evidence to support a link between the two. When we sleep our #brains become #rejuvenated and “cleaned up.” Without this restoration every night it can trigger #memory #loss. 💃🕺Lower body weight: Long-term studies have found that sleeping #five hours or less is associated with a higher risk of #obesity. Sleep helps control out #leptin levels – a hormone which signals our hunger. When leptin levels are unregulated, then we feel hungry and less satisfied, causing us to consume more calories throughout the day. On the other hand, being overweight can trigger sleep problems because it may cause sleep apnea, which is a sleep disorder categorized by snoring.💤💤💤 💤💕Enjoy your extra hour sleep🙏. I've been suffering from the flu for around 3 weeks. For most people, the flu lasts about 5-7 days and then they recover with some lingering fatigue and maybe a cough, however, because I'm immune suppressed, my body can't fight the way it should, and viruses and infections are harder for me to deal with.  I'm super careful about my exposure to viruses etc, but I have to attend medical appointments and I actually caught this flu at one of those appointments.  We initially tried tamiflu, and it helped a lot, but as soon as the course was finished the symptoms came back worse. We tried another course of tamiflu but I just wasn't getting better and it was getting dangerous.  I went to the GP who sent me to the hospital. I did blood tests and an x-ray. They were concerned about my heart rate, and although I'm already on verapamil, thought I needed a higher dose (the verapamil was initially prescribed for my cluster headaches.)  I got home around midnight last night. I am exhausted and in a tonne of pain. but I am happy to be home and hopefully on the right track to recovery.  This is why it's super important for people to get flu jabs if eligible, and to try and stay at home if you have any symptoms that may be contagious, as immune suppressed people may look just like everyone else, but we can suffer serious consequences from the most simple thing.  #chronicillnesses #chronicillnessawareness #immunesuppression #flu #influenza #fluvaccine #hospital #crohns #tachycardiaprobs

My 12 days of Christmas … Top Tip 9 My top tips for staying sane and not feeling like S..T this Christmas time … Your grandmother was right about chicken soup and scientists also agree that chicken soup will help you feel better. It’s one of the more effective feel good foods. Not only is it warm and comforting, but there are a number of substances in chicken soup that are helpful for recovery, including carnosine, which supports immune cells, and a host of vitamins and nutrients that ease mucus and inflammation in the airways. Garlic has antimicrobial and antiviral properties that relieve the common cold, I make a bruschetta with finely chopped garlic, tomatoes, sliced red onion and extra virgin oilive oil at the first sign of a lurgy. If you can’t tolerate raw garlic then you need 3 x as much cooked garlic. Try make some peri peri garlic prawns and devour several heads of garlic drenched in olive oil and chilli to ward off ills. Sweating in a hot bath or sauna can also help shift a cold and don’t forget we need plenty of fresh air too to stay well in winter months. Do try to get outside every day.  I must also highlight the importance of vitamin D, zinc and do try taking probiotics with lactobacillus if you or one of your loved ones keeps getting sick. Supplementing with all of these can help support your immune cells. Healthy gut microbes are fundamental to good immunity.  What are your hacks for warding off lurgies? SWEET AND SOUR SOUP WITH GYOZAS I haven’t been well and was crazing a sweet and spicy soup. I wasn’t going to pay £10 for one so I rummaged through the pantry and fridge and came up with this recipe  I used homemade turkey gyoza recipe. Which I will publish on here.  In the winter months this will defo be on my weekly food rotation. It was so filling but so nutritious and made me feel SO much better! You have to try this! Recipe for 2 large bowls: - 10 frozen turkey dumplings or any other dumplings  - 1 large spring onion cut fine - 1 tbsp fresh garlic, finely minced  - Kallo chicken stock cube  - X 2 OXO chicken stock cubes  - 2 pinches of ground sichuan peppercorn powder or ground  - 2 tbsp Chinese Black Sweetened Vinegar  - 2 tbsp light soy sauce  - 6 tbsp heated rapeseed oil  - 1 Pak Choi, white stems chopped  - Optional: @lkkeurope Chiu Chilli Oil to drizzle at the end 1. Bring a pot of water to the boil, add in gyozas 2. Cook on a simmer for about 8 minutes then add 0.5 cup cold water. Gyozas are done once they float to the top. Please cut into one to ensure meat is cooked  3. Between 2 soup bowls split the ingredients listed above in half: spring onions, garlic, sichuan flakes , black sweetened vinegar, soy sauce.  4. In a small pan on a low heat, add oil until starts to smoke  5. Add to the bowls and make sure you stand a bit back as it will splutter 6. In the same pan add 2 cups water and add stock cubes until dissolved.  7. Add 1 cup of broth into each bowl  8. Top with gyozas CAUTION ⛔️: The gyozas will be extremely hot so be careful when eating them #gyoza #soup #soupseason #flu #fluseason #coldandflu #mondaymotivation #mondaymood #spicysoup #leekumkee

🤧 Cold vs Flu: Decoding the Differences 🤒 🩺 Understanding the Basics: Influenza (flu) and the common cold are respiratory illnesses caused by different viruses. Flu results from influenza viruses, while the common cold can be triggered by various viruses 🤔 Key Distinctions: Flu vs Cold Intensity: In general, flu symptoms are more severe, with abrupt onset, intense discomfort, and potential serious complications. Symptoms: Both share similarities, making it challenging to differentiate based solely on symptoms. 🚨 Flu Symptoms: Fever or feeling feverish/chills Cough Sore throat Runny or stuffy nose Muscle or body aches Headaches Fatigue (tiredness) 🤒 Common Cold: Usually milder than flu More likely to have a runny or stuffy nose Rarely leads to serious health problems 💊 Treatment Approach: Common Cold: Manage symptoms with rest, fluids, and over-the-counter medications for relief. Flu: Antiviral medications can alleviate symptoms, but early intervention is crucial. Did you know that Cayenne Pepper boost Immune system support. Cayenne pepper contains high levels of vitamin C which supports immune function as vitamin C acts as an antioxidant to protect cells from damage caused by oxidative stress. Additionally, capsaicin has antimicrobial properties that can aid in the body's defence against pathogens. Research suggests that capsaicin, the active compound in cayenne pepper, can increase metabolism and promote fat burning, which may help with weight management. However, cayenne pepper alone is not a magic solution for weight loss and should be part of a overall healthy lifestyle. Cayenne pepper's spicy nature can also help stimulate mucus flow and alleviate congestion, making it useful for natural remedies for conditions like sinusitis, cough and the common cold. However, it needs to be used cautiously and in moderation, especially if you have sensitive airways. Cayenne pepper also has vasodilatory properties which means it can help widen blood vessels and improve circulation. SWEET AND SOUR SOUP WITH GYOZAS I haven’t been well and was crazing a sweet and spicy soup. I wasn’t going to pay £10 for one so I rummaged through the pantry and fridge and came up with this recipe  I used homemade turkey gyoza recipe. Which I will publish on here.  In the winter months this will defo be on my weekly food rotation. It was so filling but so nutritious and made me feel SO much better! You have to try this! Recipe for 2 large bowls: - 10 frozen turkey dumplings or any other dumplings  - 1 large spring onion cut fine - 1 tbsp fresh garlic, finely minced  - Kallo chicken stock cube  - X 2 OXO chicken stock cubes  - 2 pinches of ground sichuan peppercorn powder or ground  - 2 tbsp Chinese Black Sweetened Vinegar  - 2 tbsp light soy sauce  - 6 tbsp heated rapeseed oil  - 1 Pak Choi, white stems chopped  - Optional: @lkkeurope Chiu Chilli Oil to drizzle at the end 1. Bring a pot of water to the boil, add in gyozas 2. Cook on a simmer for about 8 minutes then add 0.5 cup cold water. Gyozas are done once they float to the top. Please cut into one to ensure meat is cooked  3. Between 2 soup bowls split the ingredients listed above in half: spring onions, garlic, sichuan flakes , black sweetened vinegar, soy sauce.  4. In a small pan on a low heat, add oil until starts to smoke  5. Add to the bowls and make sure you stand a bit back as it will splutter 6. In the same pan add 2 cups water and add stock cubes until dissolved.  7. Add 1 cup of broth into each bowl  8. Starbucks’ turmeric latte is not the one 🙅🏽‍♀️ Did you know that turmeric latte AKA haldi dudh originated in India? And the OG haldi dudh is WAYYYY more delicious and beneficial to our health than the Starbucks version. We use it as a natural home remedy for a sore throat, coughs and colds, fighting inflammation…just about anything. Turmeric is an amazing anti-inflammatory with high antioxidant levels, cancer fighting properties, anti ageing properties (hence why we smear turmeric paste on the bodies and faces of people getting married 🌝) and so much more. The main difference between real haldi dudh and Starbucks’ turmeric latte: cooking the turmeric beforehand. Skip this step and you’ll end up with the Starbucks version; it doesn’t taste good and the turmeric doesn’t mix with the milk. Cooking turmeric for a short time (30 seconds) allows it to become more soluble so it will dissolve easier into your milk and also absorb into your body easier. The anti inflammatory and antioxidant properties increase with slight cooking, and plus the flavour mellows and it tastes way better. Haldi dudh (1 cup) 1 tsp butter / ghee / coconut oil (I make mine vegan so I use coconut oil) Once melted add 1/2 tsp turmeric Cook until it browns slightly (30 seconds) and add milk of choice Ayurvedic constitution: if suitable for you, you can add spices like cinnamon and black pepper You can also add sugar, coconut sugar, maple/carob syrup etc. Never add honey to a hot drink or heat honey! When honey is heated it becomes toxic. Febre Maculosa A febre maculosa é uma doença infecciosa, febril aguda e de gravidade variável. Ela pode variar desde as formas clínicas leves e atípicas até formas graves, com elevada taxa de letalidade. A febre maculosa é causada por uma bactéria do gênero Rickettsia, transmitida pela picada do carrapato. Os principais sintomas da Febre Maculosa são: Febre alta e súbita; Cefaleia; Hiperemia conjuntival; Dor muscular e articular; Mal-estar; Dores abdominais; Vômito; Diarreia; Exantema. A Febre Maculosa, se não tratada adequadamente, pode evoluir para quadros graves e levar a pessoa à morte. Período de Incubação:  De dois a 14 dias, com média de sete dias após a picada do carrapato.  Período de Transmissibilidade:  Após a picada do carrapato, estima-se que o tempo médio necessário para que ocorra a inoculação da bactéria seja em torno de 4 a 6 horas de parasitismo, mas dependerá de cada espécie de carrapato.  Complicações: Manifestações sistêmicas que incluem edema, anasarca, insuficiência renal, manifestações neurológicas, hemorragias, miocardite, insuficiência respiratória, hipotensão e choque. Fatores de Risco  Os principais fatores de risco que aumentam as chances de se contrair a infecção por Febre Maculosa são: Viver em uma área onde a doença é comum, como locais rurais ou arborizados. Convivência com cachorro, cavalo ou outros animais domésticos. Se um carrapato infectado se prender à sua pele, é possível contrair febre maculosa ao remover o carrapato, pois o fluido do carrapato pode entrar no seu corpo por meio de uma abertura como o local da picada. Para diminuir os riscos de infecção, em caso de exposição a carrapatos, siga os seguintes passos: Ao remover um carrapato da sua pele, use uma pinça para agarrá-lo e remova-o cuidadosamente. Trate o carrapato como se estivesse contaminado: mergulhe-o em álcool ou jogue no vaso sanitário. Limpe a área da mordida com anti-séptico. Lave bem as mãos.  IMPORTANTE:  A incidência da Febre Maculosa  é mais comum em pessoas que vivem ou frequentam áreas rurais infestadas por carrapatos. além disso, estar em contato com animais como capivaras, cavalos, vacas e cachorros com carrapatos também aumenta o risco de contrair a doença. : #FebreMaculosa #Prevenção #SaúdePública #Carrapatos #SantaCatarina #dengue #flu #info  #fyp #parati #xyzbca #foryou #web #viral #fypシ #zodiacsigns #psicologi #datos #viral #blowup #real #relatable #fy

Key facts about Ibuprofen * Ibuprofen works by reducing hormones that cause pain and swelling in the body. * It takes 20 to 30 minutes to work if you take it by mouth, and 1 to 2 days to work if you put it on your skin. * Ibuprofen is typically used for period pain or toothache. Some people find ibuprofen better than paracetamol for back pain. * Always take ibuprofen tablets, capsules, granules and liquid with food or a drink of milk to reduce the chance of an upset stomach. Do not take it on an empty stomach. * If you're taking tablets, capsules, granules or liquid, take the lowest dose to control your pain for the shortest possible time. Do not take it for more than 10 days (or 3 days if you're under 18) unless you've spoken to your doctor. Max’s story…. 41 days living in 3 different hospitals as a family, there have been some dark days as our little boy has fought Influenza A, Pneumotharaces, and lots lots more. And after over 3 weeks sedated, to see Max coming out the other side of all this in the last couple of weeks full of determination and all with that cheeky grin on his face makes us unbelievably proud and full of more love than we ever thought possible. There is still a way to go with Max’s rehab but he is improving immensely every day. Considering the amount his body has been through, we have never been happier for being given the runaround! Tried to keep track of a few numbers…  - 41 days in hospital - 26 different visitors - 14 hospital bed spaces - 12 chest x-rays - 10 Toy Story marathons - 8 new cuddly toys - 6 types of breathing support - 5 days on ECMO life support - 4 ambulance journeys - 3 hospitals - 2 chest drains - 1 new baby brother!! (in a pear tree!?) - ALSO… 1 unbelievable NHS - it get’s some stick but my word it’s filled with some incredible people. We’re eternally grateful for everything they’ve done for Max and supporting us at QMC, Leicester Royal Infirmary and Kings Mill.  We can’t thank our family and friends enough for all the support you’ve given us. Whether it’s doing our washing, bringing us food, looking after Otis, or simply sending a quick text to check in, you have helped us get through what I hope proves to be one of the hardest thing we’ll experience as a family. Now it’s time to fully enjoy life as our family of 4 and make the most of the rest of Richard’s paternity leave all together! ❤️ #family #hospital #Maxsstory #influenza #recovery #toddler #viral #trend #foryou #foryoupage #fyp #xyzbca

Thank you to the vast majority of people who have been very kind ideed. It was lovely to feel supported while i was alone in a&e, for the most part feeling dreadful, and at points when i was told my bloods were abnormal- feeling pretty worried- and by myself for the 11 hour stay- im very grateful to you.  There have been a load of comments telling me theres nothing wrong with me if i’m on my phone, that i only have flu and should have seen my GP (i did see him- he was the one that sent me there), and generally disgnosing my condition off the back of a 3 minute video. Numerous of other types of comments listed in video, which i also address.  To those people- i hope this answers your questions.  The doctors and nurses i saw were wll absolutely amazing, and im extremely grateful to them for getting to the bottom of why ive had these syptoms for so long. I do indeed have flu, but i also have typhoid- this is something i had 16 months ago and was treated with antibiotics successful for. Theu have found the specific typhoid i have is a “colonising typhoid”, which means it stays dormamt within your system forever, and mutates and flares up with triggers- in this case the flu. I’m being treated again with antibiotics. I also have severe mineral deficiencies- potassium, calcium and magnesium due to the constant dihorrea, and those have been making my legs feel worse and worse and caused all the shaking etc. i can now take supplements for these until i can eat again. Lastly, i also have a UTI, but in the grand scheme of things, its not a huge issue.  So, for those of you who’ve been umpleasant, hopefully this answers your questions. Please comsider how comments such as yours make someone feel, and if you really need to be saying something not nice? There are plenty of other accounts to follow if you dont like mine.  Again- very grateful to all of you who have been so kind. Grandma vs Science: Garlic for Colds? #natural. Garlic, a pungent member of the lily family, isn't just a flavor booster in your kitchen. It boasts a rich history of medicinal use and potential health benefits backed by modern science. A Journey Through Time: Garlic as Medicine Ancient Uses: Evidence suggests garlic's medicinal properties were recognized as early as 3,000 BC. Egyptians, Greeks, Romans, and Chinese cultures all incorporated it into their healing practices, believing it could ward off illness, improve circulation, and treat wounds. The Plague Years: During the Middle Ages, garlic was used as a preventative measure against the bubonic plague, thought to purify the blood and ward off evil spirits (which were then believed to cause disease). Modern Science Takes Hold: While the evil spirit theory fell out of favor, scientific research continues to explore garlic's potential health benefits. Modern Science on Garlic's Benefits: Immune System Support: Garlic contains allicin, a compound with potential antibiotic and antiviral properties. Studies suggest it might help reduce the severity and duration of the common cold [1]. Heart Health: Garlic may help lower blood pressure and improve cholesterol levels, potentially reducing the risk of heart disease [2]. Other Potential Benefits: Research is ongoing, but garlic may also have benefits for blood sugar control, reducing inflammation, and even certain types of cancer, though more evidence is needed [3]. Important Note: While garlic is generally safe for most people in culinary amounts, it can interact with certain medications and cause side effects in high doses. It's always best to consult your doctor before using garlic for medicinal purposes. Conclusion: Garlic's journey from ancient remedy to a subject of scientific study highlights its potential to promote health. While more research is needed to fully understand its effects, incorporating garlic into your diet can be a delicious way to support your overall well-being. #garlic #flu

Sepsis and the flu are two serious medical conditions that can share some similar symptoms, leading to confusion among individuals. Sepsis is a life-threatening condition that occurs when the body's response to an infection causes inflammation throughout the body, potentially leading to organ failure. On the other hand, the flu is a viral infection that primarily affects the respiratory system and can cause symptoms such as fever, cough, and body aches. The confusion between sepsis and the flu often arises because both conditions can present with symptoms like fever, chills, fatigue, and body aches. However, there are key differences between the two that make it crucial to differentiate them accurately. Misidentifying sepsis as the flu can be dangerous for several reasons. Sepsis requires prompt medical attention and treatment with antibiotics and supportive care to prevent serious complications and potentially fatal outcomes. Delaying or failing to treat sepsis promptly can lead to septic shock, organ failure, and even death. It is essential to be aware of the differences between sepsis and the flu and to seek medical attention if you suspect sepsis, especially if you have a known infection or are at higher risk for developing sepsis. Quick and accurate diagnosis is crucial for initiating appropriate treatment and improving outcomes for individuals with sepsis. If you or someone you know is experiencing symptoms that could indicate sepsis, such as high fever, rapid heart rate, confusion, or difficulty breathing, do not hesitate to seek immediate medical help. Remember, early recognition and treatment of sepsis can save lives. #sepsis #sepsissurvivor #flu #influenza #fyp

“Feed a Cold and Starve a Fever” #wait. The old adage "feed a cold and starve a fever" has been passed down through generations, but modern medical understanding suggests that this advice is more myth than fact. Both colds and fevers are symptoms of infections that place additional demands on the body, requiring balanced and adequate nutrition for effective recovery. When dealing with a cold, it's crucial to maintain a well-rounded diet to support the immune system. Nutrient-rich foods, hydration, and rest help the body combat the virus and recover more efficiently. Eating healthily can provide the necessary vitamins and minerals, such as vitamin C and zinc, which are known to boost immune function. Similarly, when experiencing a fever, the body’s metabolism increases, burning more calories and requiring more fluids. Adequate nutrition and hydration are essential to support the body's increased energy needs and to replace fluids lost through sweating. While a fever might reduce appetite, consuming easily digestible foods like soups, fruits, and vegetables can help maintain energy levels and provide the necessary nutrients. #healthcare #sick #ill #flu

Scientists have discovered a simple and effective remedy for reducing the duration of colds in children - saline nasal drops.  *Here are the key findings: Study Results Using saline nasal drops cut the duration of colds in children by an average of 2 days. Children using the drops had cold symptoms for about 6 days, compared to 8 days with usual care. The drops also reduced transmission to other family members - 46% of households reported spread with drops vs 61% with usual care. How It Works The salt solution provides extra chloride to cells lining the nose and airways. This helps the cells produce more hypochlorous acid, which suppresses viral replication. As a result, the viral infection is shortened, reducing symptom duration. **Usage and Availability Parents can safely make and administer the drops at home. The recommended dosage is 3 drops per nostril at least 4 times daily until recovery. **Over-the-counter saline drops are available for as little as £1.30, with branded options around £4.70. **Additional Benefits Children using the drops needed fewer other medicines during illness. 82% of parents said the drops helped their child recover faster. 81% said they would use the drops for future colds. This simple, inexpensive remedy offers parents an effective way to shorten their children's colds and reduce spread within households. The researchers plan to release instructions soon for parents to make the solution at home. Teachers tend to get more colds and other illnesses due to several factors, including: 1. **Increased Exposure**: Teachers are in close contact with many students each day, increasing their exposure to germs. 2. **Touching Surfaces**: Classrooms can be breeding grounds for bacteria and viruses since students frequently touch desks, toys, and other shared surfaces. 3. **Stress and Fatigue**: The demands of teaching can lead to stress and fatigue, which may compromise the immune system. 4. **Seasonal Factors**: The winter months when colds are more common also coincide with school sessions, leading to a higher likelihood of transmission. 5. **Air Quality**: Classrooms can have poor ventilation, making it easier for germs to linger in the air. Here are five ways teachers can help prevent themselves from picking up germs in the classroom: 1. **Regular Hand Washing**: Frequently washing hands with soap and water, especially before eating and after using the restroom, can greatly reduce the likelihood of transmission. 2. **Use Hand Sanitizer**: Keeping hand sanitizer available in the classroom for quick clean-ups after touching shared items can help kill germs. 3. **Disinfect Surfaces**: Regularly cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces such as desks, doorknobs, and shared equipment can reduce the spread of germs. 4. **Encourage Healthy Habits**: Teaching students about proper hygiene practices, such as coughing into elbows and not sharing personal items, can help minimize germ transmission. #teachersoftiktok #teacherhack #coldremedies #colds #flu #healthyliving #teacher #teacherstruggles #hotwater #coldrelief #staysafeguys #immuneboost #immunesystem #teacherlife

Tired of flu symptoms? Fermented Honey Garlic Instructions: Add garlic to a clean jar and raw honey. let it ferment on counter for 4-6 weeks. ❤️ FAQs: 1. Do I need to refrigerate it? — No, if done correctly, fermented honey garlic is shelf-stable. You can leave it on the counter until you use it all. 2. Can I use pre-peeled garlic from the store? — I wouldn’t recommend it as pre-peeled garlic may have been pasteurized, which could hinder fermentation. 3. What kind of honey should I use? — Use RAW honey, regardless of its color. 4. What should I expect during fermentation? —In 1-3 weeks, you may notice bubbles forming (a good sign of fermentation), honey becoming runnier each day, gas inside the jar (burping and flipping are important here), and some messes if honey spills (leave some headspace to avoid this). 5. Do I have to see bubbles in the first two weeks? — Not necessarily. It depends on the garlic-to-honey ratio. I recommend adding enough honey to cover all the garlic to ensure fermentation. 6. My honey has crystallized. What should I do? — Stir the honey and try a warm water bath. 7. My garlic is turning green. Is that normal? — Yes, it’s normal. It may eventually turn golden. 8. My garlic cloves are floating on top. Is that normal? — Yes, it’s normal for the first 2-4 weeks of fermentation. Flip and burp the jar daily for 10 seconds. You can also cut the cloves in halves and slightly bruise them to speed up the process. 9. How do I consume the honey and garlic? — You can start using the honey at the 3-4 week mark. Once the garlic cloves turn golden, you can try them. If they’re too spicy, wait a little longer for a sweeter taste. Enjoy them on bread, in salad dressings, or sautéed with veggies. 10.How can I prevent botulism? — Add a splash of apple cider vinegar (ACV) at any point during fermentation. While botulism is rare, this can provide peace of mind. #flu #cold #immuneboost #holistichealth #fyp

A Bournemouth mother has told of the horror of watching her daughter's 'stomach flu' spiral into a life-threatening illness that has ultimately left her disabled. Two year-old Iyla-Mae returned home from nursery one afternoon in July with what appeared to be a vomiting bug — which was not uncommon for the young child.  But, unlike previous occasions, the vomiting persisted and four days later Iyla-Mae woke up in hysterical tears, unable to move. Her mother, 27 year-old Paige Coneley, called the NHS 111 helpline, who advised her to take the little girl straight to A&E. Doctors took CT scans of her brain and spotted signs she was suffering seizures. Iyla-Mae was blue-lighted to a specialist unit at Southampton General Hospital where doctors confirmed she had suffered cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — a rare form of stroke that affects about one in 100,000 people a year and is especially prevalent in children. The condition, CVST, causes a blood clot to form in the network of channels in the brain that are responsible for draining liquid.  The blockage had caused damage to the delicate blood vessels, leading to swelling and bleeding in the brain. This chain of events is part of a stroke, where the supply of oxygenated blood to the brain is obstructed, causing significant neurological damage.  Doctors are unclear as to whether Iyla Mae's vomiting bug was a pre-cursor or cause of the stroke.  However studies show that prolonged and projectile vomiting can cause extreme hikes in blood pressure, contributing to the formation of blood clots.  It is also known that vomiting, as well as drowsiness, seizures and problems with walking can be initial warning signs of a stroke.  Ms Coneley said the extent of her daughter's brain damage was such that she had to 'learn how to do everything again, from scratch'.  In mid-July, the toddler underwent an operation to reduce the fluid on her brain and remained in intensive care for four days before being moved to the neurosurgical ward at Southampton Children's Hospital where she stayed for 17 weeks. Doctors warned Ms Coneley that there was a possibility of a second stroke and more bleeding on the brain. The news was devastating: Ms Coneley 'collapsed on the floor by her bed' and 'cried'. She told MailOnline: 'I got a chair and sat by her bed, held her hand and whispered in her ear "mummy needs you more than you need me come on baby girl".' 'I closed my eyes and all I could picture was me planning her funeral,' she added.  Following the successful operation Iyla-Mae was put on blood thinners and anti-seizure medication for six months and started undergoing intense rehabilitation.  'They've helped her to gain some control of her head, but sometimes it flops down,' said Ms Coneley. Therapy aimed to help her sit and stand, but she needed to be supported at all times.   Other rehabilitation tasks included teaching Iyla-Mae how to 'push buttons' on her toys.  Speech and language experts also checked to see how well she could swallow. In  September she became able to swallow yoghurt, which was some improvement. But Ms Coneley said her sucking reflex hasn't come back, meaning she is not yet able to drink water from a bottle. A Canadian teenager is hospitalized in critical condition with suspected bird flu, health officials reported Tuesday. The teen has been receiving care at BC Children’s Hospital in Vancouver since Friday, the same day an initial test came back positive for H5 influenza. The young person’s first symptoms, which began a week before they were hospitalized, were conjunctivitis or red eyes, fever and cough, Henry said. The illness has progressed to acute respiratory distress syndrome, or ARDS. People with ARDS typically need help breathing with machines such as a ventilator, but officials did not offer specifics on the teen’s treatment except to say they’re receiving antiviral medications. This appears to be the first known human case of bird flu acquired in Canada. The country had one case in 2014, which was travel-related, Henry said. It is still unknown how the teen caught this strain of flu, which has been circulating widely in wild birds, poultry and some mammals, including cattle in North America since 2022. “Because this is such a rare event and a sentinel event, it is important for us to do as thorough an investigation as possible, and we’re committed to doing that,” Henry said. There have also been 46 confirmed human infections in the United States as part of the ongoing outbreak this year, mostly among farm workers tending infected animals. All those cases have been mild, and people who have tested positive have recovered from their illnesses after treatment with antiviral medications. Canadian officials are following more than 40 people who had contact with the teen during their infectious period, which started two days before they began experiencing symptoms. “I will also say that there are many other tests that are being done on a number of people across the province to try and really get an understanding of what’s happening here,” Henry said. So far, officials have no other evidence of anyone else becoming ill after contact with the teen. “We don’t see right now that there’s a risk of a lot of people being sick,” she said. More than two dozen poultry farms in British Columbia have been affected by H5N1, Henry said. Since 2022, about 11 million birds have been destroyed, with most of them in British Columbia. Unlike in the US, H5N1 has not been detected dairy cattle or milk in Canada. “We are looking very, very carefully at all potential animal exposures, bird exposures. There were other pets in the house, and there was contact with pets in other houses,” Henry said. The teen had contact with dogs, cats and reptiles, but none has tested positive for H5N1. Investigators have not identified any contact between the teen and birds. “This is a tragic development. It is an unfortunately unsurprising development,” said Dr. Jennifer Nuzzo, who directs the Pandemic Center at the Brown University School of Public Health. “I think there’s been a lot of wishful thinking about this virus, that it wouldn’t cause people to become severely ill, but that hope, really, I think, stands in contrast to several decades worth of data,” she said. Since 2003, over 900 human cases of H5N1 have been reported to the World Health Organization. Slightly more than half have been fatal. “What I think this absolutely underscores is that H5N1 is a very serious public health threat, and we need to be doing more to stay ahead of it, to prevent more people from becoming severely ill or die,” Nuzzo said. #canada🇨🇦 #teenboy #critical #condition #suspect #bird #flu #children #hospital #vancouver #initial #influenza #symptoms #illness #human #case #caught #rare #infection #unitedstates #outbreak #investigation #fever #cough #eyes #red #cattle #syndrome #travel #worker #antiviral #farms #mild #tested #medicine #mammal #dozen #british #colombia #poultry #dairy #milk #animal #care #dogs #bird #fatal #serious #public #publichealth #data #treat #news #breakingnews #usa🇺🇸 #unitedkingdom

Here’s what Ayurveda recommends for staying balanced: 1.	Warm, Moist Foods: Opt for soups, stews, and dishes with root vegetables, ghee, and warming spices like ginger, cinnamon, and turmeric. Skip cold salads and raw foods, which can disrupt digestion. 2.	Cover Key Areas: Keep your neck, feet, and ears warm. These areas help preserve your body’s core heat and protect you from winter imbalances. 3.	Stay Hydrated: Drink warm water or herbal teas with cumin, fennel, or cardamom to keep digestion strong and prevent dryness. Avoid ice-cold drinks or too much caffeine. 4.	Daily Oil Massage: Use warm sesame oil to massage your body (especially joints and feet). This reduces dryness, calms the nervous system, and keeps your skin healthy. 5.	Support Digestion: Begin your day with a pinch of ginger and Himalayan salt under your tongue, or have it as tea. This boosts your digestive fire, essential in winter. 6.	Sleep Well: Wind down with warm milk infused with nutmeg or ashwagandha for better immunity and deeper sleep. Small, consistent habits can help you thrive this winter. Flu is one of the illnesses circulating in the UK that have been dubbed the "quad-demic". England's chief medical officer Chris Whitty is urging those eligible to get vaccinated. Cases of winter flu are "rising rapidly" - with England's health boss urging those eligible to get vaccinated. Cases are highest among those aged five to 14, with 16.9% of tests positive for flu - up from 11.5% last week. Sharing the data on X, England's chief medical officer Professor Chris Whitty said: "Influenza is now rising rapidly. Antiviral flu medicines can now be used in primary care." "If you are eligible please get vaccinated." The number of cases is in line with the 2022 to 2023 season, which peaked on 20 December, with 33% of tests positive for flu. Last year, the peak was much smaller - with 16.7% of tests positive - and came more than a month later, on 27 January. #winter #flu #2025 #winterflu #healthy #fy #fyp #coronavirus #flujab #newsbuzz247
